title: Jones polynomial approximation

problem.name: Jones polynomial approximation
problem.statement_latex:
\textbf{Jones polynomial of a plat closure.} Given an $n$-strand braid $b$ of length $m$, a permitted root of unity $t=e^{2\pi i/k}$ and $\varepsilon>0$, estimate the Jones polynomial of its plat closure to the additive scale $\varepsilon d^{n/2-1}$, where $d=2\cos(\pi/k)$. Complexity is in the finite braid description.

\textbf{Jones polynomial of a trace closure.} Given a braid and a permitted fixed root of unity, estimate the Jones polynomial of its trace closure to inverse-polynomial additive error after the Markov-trace normalization. Input and output are finite braid data and a numerical estimate.

quantum.headline_latex: \textbf{Jones polynomial of a plat closure.} $\operatorname{poly}(n,m,k,1/\varepsilon)$ quantum time by Aharonov--Jones--Landau, using the path-model braid representation and a Hadamard test.
quantum.details_latex: \textbf{Jones polynomial of a trace closure.} $\operatorname{poly}(n,m,1/\varepsilon)$ time in the one-clean-qubit model by Shor--Jordan, using normalized-trace estimation of the path-model braid representation.

classical.headline_latex: \textbf{Jones polynomial of a plat closure.} Classical tensor contraction or state-vector evaluation takes $\exp(O(n))\operatorname{poly}(m,k,1/\varepsilon)$ time, with width-dependent improvements. At universal fixed roots and inverse-polynomial normalized error, efficient classical approximation would imply $\mathsf{BQP}=\mathsf{BPP}$. For an implemented $q$-qubit, $g$-gate circuit over a fixed finite algebraic gate set, classical simulation also gives $\min\{O(g2^q),\operatorname{poly}(g)2^{O(w)},\operatorname{poly}(s)2^{O(s/\sqrt{\log s})}\}$. Here $w$ is a contraction width and $s$ is the size of the sparse bounded-fan-in Boolean encoding of scalar path counts at the required precision; gate synthesis and precision contribute to $g,s$.
classical.details_latex: \textbf{Jones polynomial of a trace closure.} General exact contraction is exponential in braid width. A polynomial-time classical algorithm for the complete normalized approximation regime would place $\mathsf{DQC1}$ inside $\mathsf{BPP}$. For an implemented $q$-qubit, $g$-gate circuit over a fixed finite algebraic gate set, classical simulation also gives $\min\{O(g2^q),\operatorname{poly}(g)2^{O(w)},\operatorname{poly}(s)2^{O(s/\sqrt{\log s})}\}$. Here $w$ is a contraction width and $s$ is the size of the sparse bounded-fan-in Boolean encoding of scalar path counts at the required precision; gate synthesis and precision contribute to $g,s$.
